subject: Test if ggplot object have already been rendered?

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Test if ggplot object have already been rendered?
parts:
Hi,

in R.utils v1.9.3 I have toPNG() etc that opens a PNG device (also
toPDF(), toEPS() etc), evaluates some code and then (guarantees) to
close the device, all in a device-independent fashion, e.g.

library("R.utils");
library("ggplot2");

toPNG("MyPlot", aspectRatio=0.7, {
gg <- qplot(rating, data=movies, geom="histogram");
print(gg);
})

I'd like to adjust toPNG() et al. such you can *also* do without the
explicit print(<ggplot>):

toPNG("MyPlot", aspectRatio=0.7, {
qplot(rating, data=movies, geom="histogram");
})

I'd like to support both the explicit and the implicit approach. Is
there a way to detect whether print(gg) have already been called, so
that toPNG() will only call print(gg) if needed. I certainly don't
want to call it twice, e.g.

toPNG("MyPlot2", aspectRatio=0.7, {
gg <- qplot(rating, data=movies, geom="histogram");
print(gg);
print(gg);
})

Thanks,

Henrik

messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: Re: Test if ggplot object have already been rendered?
parts:
Hi Henrik,

Two ideas come to mind, but neither seems "good". One, you could
query the display list. For example:

grid:::grid.Call("L_getDLelt", 1L)

but I do not know from this alone how you could guarantee that what
was there was the graph. What would happen in a case like this?

toPNG("MyPlot", aspectRatio=0.7, {
gg <- qplot(rating, data=movies, geom="histogram");
print(gg);

gg2 <- qplot(1:10)
})

second, you could parse the expression for calls to print in the last position:

f <- function(x, expr) {
d <- substitute(expr)
p <- grepl("print\\(", d)
if (!p[length(p)]) {
print()
} else dev.off()
}

Of course, if the user is using a function that prints, but is not
called print, this does not work, or if they do something like:

p <- qplot(1:10)
print(p)
cat("done")

in which case you could just search for print occuring anywhere, but
then what about my first case?

Hope this helps at least some,

Cheers,

Josh

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Test if ggplot object have already been rendered?
parts:
Hi,

Another idea: overwrite print.ggplot to keep track of whether it has
been called or not,

print.ggplot <- function(x, ...) {
ggplot2:::print.ggplot(x, ...)
.printed <<- TRUE
}

( p = qplot(1,1) )
if( ! .printed ) print(p)

HTH,

baptiste
